paragraphs.text: A **cash-secured put** is a short put position in which the writer sets aside enough cash to buy the shares at the strike price if the put is assigned [S1]. The writer sells the put, collects the premium up front, and accepts the obligation to buy 100 shares per contract at the strike any time before expiration [S1]. The word *secured* refers to the cash: in a cash account the broker holds the full purchase price (strike × 100, less the premium received) as collateral for the whole life of the trade [S1]. **Assignment** is the process by which an option writer is selected to fulfil the obligation of a contract that a holder has exercised [S2].

Buying power of {{profile.buying_power|money}} was split with a tilt of {{allocation.tilt}}: {{allocation.csp_pct|pct}} to cash-secured puts and {{allocation.cash_pct|pct}} held as cash. The regime was labelled {{regime.label}}, with a VIX of {{regime.vix}} at the {{regime.vix_percentile}}th percentile.

The **Cboe Volatility Index (VIX)** measures the market's expectation of 30-day volatility in the S&P 500, derived from the prices of a wide strip of S&P 500 index options [S5]. It is quoted as an annualised percentage: a VIX of 20 implies an expected one-month move of roughly ±5.8% in the index (20% divided by the square root of 12) [S5]. Because it is computed from option prices rather than from past returns, the VIX moves with fear and relief in real time, rising sharply in sell-offs and drifting down in calm markets, which earned it the nickname "fear gauge" [S5].

The good-to-own quality screen is a filter, not a discovery engine: it decides which tickers are allowed into the option screeners at all, records a reason for every rejection, and produces a score for the survivors. Here, {{quality_screen.passed_count}} underlyings passed: {{quality_screen.passed_tickers|list}}.

The quality gate enforces the product promise of "stocks you would be happy to own if assigned" [S3]. It is a filter, not a discovery engine: it decides which tickers are allowed into the option screeners at all, records a reason for every rejection, and produces a score for the survivors [S3].

The trend board is a secondary signal only, re-ordering quality-gated stocks rather than adding any. Trending entities such as CAVA and ONON scored highly but were excluded because they are not on the good-to-own list.

The app watches public conversation on Reddit, X, Wikipedia pageviews, Google Trends and news feeds for rising discussion of products and brands, resolves that discussion to tickers, and produces a consumer-trend score [S4]. It would be natural to assume a stock with a surging score is a good candidate for selling puts, but for the structure of a short put, the opposite is closer to the truth [S4].

The bottleneck board is a secondary signal only: it re-orders quality-gated stocks, never adds one. The top layer was Power generation and grid equipment with a score of {{bottlenecks.layers[0].score}} and thesis state {{bottlenecks.layers[0].thesis_state}}.

Next to every short put this app shows a **probability OTM**: the model's estimate of the chance that the option finishes out of the money at expiration and therefore expires worthless, which for a cash-secured put writer is the outcome in which the whole premium is kept and no shares are bought [S6].
